claims.text: As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a density of 10.21 g cm−3.
Selective laser sintering can introduce pores into HfMoTaTiZr.
Introducing pores will reduce the overall density of HfMoTaTiZr.
A sufficient load-bearing cross-sectional area can allow porous HfMoTaTiZr to retain its strength.
Pore-induced toughening mechanisms may help porous HfMoTaTiZr maintain mechanical properties.
Selective-laser-sintered porous HfMoTaTiZr will have lower density than as-cast HfMoTaTiZr.
Selective-laser-sintered porous HfMoTaTiZr will maintain or improve its mechanical properties at room temperature relative to the as-cast alloy.
Selective-laser-sintered porous HfMoTaTiZr will maintain or improve its mechanical properties at temperatures up to 1000 °C relative to the as-cast alloy.
The proposed property retention applies under tensile, compressive, and impact loading.
The density reduction and mechanical-property retention depend on pore size, pore distribution, and pore volume fraction.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis requires density reduction without sacrificing mechanical properties, but the rejection rule requires both a mechanical-property loss greater than 10% and a density reduction below 5%. Consequently, a greater-than-10% property loss accompanied by a density reduction of at least 5% would not falsify the stated rule even though it contradicts the no-sacrifice hypothesis.
